finding.evidence: DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200
finding.description: Database, mail and payment secrets are public.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: exposed-secrets (Database, mail and payment secrets are public. Evidence: DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Recommended fix for exposed DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200: treat as compromise - immediately revoke and rotate all 3 secrets upstream, remove secrets from all client-visible output (API HTTP 200 responses, HTML, JS bundles, config endpoints), move them to server-side secrets management / vault with restricted IAM and authentication/authorization, require TLS for transport, and enable logging/accounting with short-lived credentials and rotation. Per OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet.

sources.contribution: Section 2.8 is Transport Layer Security (TLS) Everywhere

verification.claim: Section 2.8 is Transport Layer Security (TLS) Everywhere

fix.summary: Block secret disclosure by serving the normal catalogue page with 404 instead of .env contents.
fix.risk: Direct /.env requests no longer return secrets; catalogue rendering reused so journeys unaffected.
